cases.expected_description: curl E = +i w B and curl H = -i w D + J
cases.name: b4.convention.maxwell_signs_recorded
cases.notes: signs from a source using e^{+i omega t} are NOT copied. Mixing the two gives a medium that looks passive but propagates as if it had gain, and the equations stay self-consistent, so no residual would catch it -- the vacuum case below is what pins them
cases.reference: the frequency-domain curl equations are recorded and derived from this project's own e^{-i omega t} kernel

cases.name: b4.vacuum.plane_wave_dispersion
cases.notes: measured as ||M v|| for the known mode, NOT as a smallest singular value: the latter goes through M^dagger M and its square root amplifies a 1e-16 eigenvalue error to 1e-8
cases.reference: |k| = omega in vacuum with c = 1: the analytic transverse mode is annihilated by the plane-wave operator exactly on the light cone

cases.expected_description: smallest singular value well away from zero off the cone
cases.name: b4.vacuum.off_shell_is_not_singular
cases.reference: at |k| = 1.7 omega the operator is NOT singular, so the previous case is not passing for a trivial reason

cases.name: b4.isotropic.analytic_dispersion
cases.reference: |k|^2 = eps mu omega^2 for an isotropic medium, with H_z = sqrt(eps/mu) E_y

cases.name: b4.isotropic.phase_velocity
cases.reference: v_p = 1/sqrt(eps mu)

cases.expected_description: both divergences and the Faraday relation vanish
cases.name: b4.vacuum.transversality_and_curl
cases.notes: this is the case that pins the sign of the Faraday equation: with the opposite kernel it would read k x E = -omega H
cases.reference: k.E = k.H = 0 and k x E = omega H for the vacuum transverse mode

cases.name: b4.fresnel.vacuum_factorizes_into_the_light_cone
cases.notes: det W vanishes identically because W annihilates k on both sides, so the physics is in the adjugate. That it comes out rank one, and a perfect square, is the statement that vacuum has a single light cone and no birefringence
cases.reference: the Fresnel quartic from adj(W) = lambda k (x) k is proportional to (eta^{ab} k_a k_b)^2, with ONE constant across every wavevector

cases.name: b4.fresnel.conformal_invariance_of_the_cone
cases.reference: the Fresnel scalar is unchanged under g_eff -> Omega^2 g_eff, so the light cone is a property of the conformal class

cases.expected_description: degenerate for the metric medium, split for the generic one
cases.name: b4.fresnel.metric_media_do_not_birefringe
cases.notes: the second half is the point: NOT every reciprocal medium corresponds to one effective metric. A quartic that does not factorize into a doubled quadric describes two distinct cones, and eps = diag(2, 3.5, 5) is such a medium
cases.reference: a metric-induced medium has its two propagation branches degenerate, while a generic reciprocal anisotropic medium splits them

cases.name: b4.group_velocity_matches_finite_differences
cases.notes: two independent routes through the same dispersion relation
cases.reference: v_g = dw/dk from the dispersion curve equals c/(n + w dn/dw)

cases.name: b4.poynting_vacuum
cases.reference: <S> = (1/2) Re[E x conj(H)] gives energy flow along +x with magnitude 1/2 for a unit vacuum transverse mode

cases.name: b4.magnetoelectric_directional_asymmetry
cases.notes: zeta = z K is the moving-medium form, so this is Fresnel drag and not a sign error. It is also why wavevector, phase-velocity and energy-flow directions must not be assumed to coincide
cases.reference: in a magnetoelectric medium the forward and backward wavenumbers differ in magnitude: phase velocity is direction dependent

cases.name: b4.layered.lossless_slab_conserves_energy
cases.notes: R and T come from the scattering matrix independently; this is not a definition
cases.reference: R + T = 1 for a lossless dielectric slab

cases.name: b4.layered.lossless_slab_absorbs_nothing
cases.reference: the independently integrated dissipated power is zero in a lossless slab

cases.name: b4.layered.lossy_slab_energy_balance
cases.notes: A is computed INDEPENDENTLY of R and T, so this is a genuine balance. Setting A = 1 - R - T and then asserting the sum is 1 would be circular
cases.reference:
R + T + A = 1 with A obtained by integrating

= (w/2) Im[E* D + H* B] through the internal field profile

cases.name: b4.layered.absorption_is_positive_for_a_passive_slab
cases.reference: a passive lossy slab absorbs a strictly positive amount of power

cases.expected_description: gain detected, and the balance still closes
cases.name: b4.layered.active_slab_is_detected
cases.notes: the energy balance closing on a NEGATIVE absorption is the strongest form of this check: the sign is physical, not clamped
cases.reference: a slab with Im eps < 0 shows NEGATIVE absorption and R + T > 1

cases.name: b4.layered.thick_evanescent_stack_is_stable
cases.notes: this is why scattering matrices were used rather than transfer matrices: the latter carry e^{|Im k| d} for the backward wave and overflow long before the physics goes wrong
cases.reference: a 40-unit evanescent layer returns finite R and T with T exponentially small, rather than overflowing

cases.expected_description: a measurable phase difference, with energy conserved in both
cases.name: b4.propagation.restricted_family_costs_phase
cases.notes: this quantifies the PROPAGATION cost of a constitutive approximation, which a tensor-norm residual alone does not. Both profiles are lossless, so R + T = 1 holds for each
cases.reference: dropping the magnetoelectric term changes measurable propagation observables -- phase accumulation and group delay -- through a warp-analogue profile, and both stacks conserve energy

cases.computed_description: coarse (21 samples): min eig = -3.1308e+01 at w = 3.0500e+00; adaptive (981 samples, 6 rounds): min eig = -4.9965e+02 at w = 3.0558e+00; resonances targeted: 3, mu zeros: 2
cases.expected_description: a strictly lower minimum found by refinement
cases.name: b4.adaptive.refines_the_passivity_margin
cases.notes: BOTH results are reported, coarse and refined, because the difference between them is the measure of what a fixed grid misses. The refined scan narrows the unverified region; it does NOT prove global passivity, which would need an analytic positive-real argument this project has not carried out
cases.reference: the adaptive scan finds a strictly LOWER minimum loss eigenvalue than the coarse grid, by refining around resonances, zeros of det mu and local minima

cases.name: b4.hypad.propagation_phase_gradient
cases.notes: evaluated away from any eigenvalue degeneracy or branch crossing, where the observable is smooth. Differentiating through branch sorting or discrete mode selection is NOT done here, and would have to be documented as non-smooth if it were
cases.reference: d(phase)/d(eps) through a slab matches the analytic w d /(2 sqrt(eps))

cases.name: b4.deterministic_repeatability
cases.reference: two identical stack solves return bit-identical R, T and A

cases.expected_description: at least two real branches for an anisotropic medium
cases.name: b4.branch_count_is_reported
cases.notes: where two branches approach each other any mode-sorting derivative is non-smooth, which is why the HyPAD case above is evaluated away from degeneracies and says so
cases.reference: the number of real propagation branches along a direction is counted and reported rather than assumed

title: B4-MAXWELL-PROPAGATION: does the B3 constitutive model produce the electromagnetic propagation the target effective metric predicts? Plane-wave operator, Fresnel polynomial, layered propagation and energy balance
